headline: Drupal flaws and ten CISA-listed exploited bugs need patching; most federal deadlines fall on 28 November
plain_summary: Drupal says two flaws in its core software are being used in attacks, and CISA added ten exploited flaws to its catalogue, most with federal deadlines on 28 November. A Linux file-server flaw and tampered installers of two Windows tools also need attention. SAP confirmed suspicious activity, but says it has found no evidence customer business data was accessed. Check Drupal sites and the listed products.

items.title: Drupal core flaw CVE-2026-132165 exploited; CISA deadline is today
items.why: Drupal reports exploitation on live sites, CISA lists it as exploited, and a public proof of concept is reported.
items.action: Drupal advises updating core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13; if you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes.

items.title: Second Drupal core flaw, CVE-2026-136716, exploited
items.why: Drupal says the access bypass is being exploited and sites with an open installer may already be compromised.
items.action: Drupal advises updating to the fixed version for your release line and running update.php, securing the installer, and checking logs for unauthorized access, especially to the user 1 account.

items.title: CISA adds ten exploited flaws: Mitel, Xen Orchestra, Juniper, Danfoss
items.why: Eight have a federal due date of 28 November; Mitel flaws were reportedly exploited as zero-days.
items.action: CISA's catalog entries say to apply vendor mitigations as BOD 26-04 requires, or stop using the product if none are available; Mitel advises its fixed MiCollab release and restricting external access to the conferencing component, per Infobae.

items.title: Linux NFS server flaw NFS2ROOT (CVE-2026-99362) could give remote root
items.why: It is reachable over the network when nfsd is exposed; no exploitation in the wild is reported and fixed kernels exist.
items.action: General advice: apply your distribution's kernel update and reboot; if you cannot, restrict access to the NFS port to trusted clients, or stop and disable the nfs-server service if it is not needed.

items.title: Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers on the official site were tampered with
items.why: AhnLab says the files install a Python remote access trojan; the cause of the replacement is not identified.
items.action: AhnLab advises checking SHA-256 hashes against the official page, reinstalling the latest version, and checking for suspicious Python environments, scheduled tasks and external traffic; reinstalling alone may not remove the RAT.

items.title: PolinRider loader reported in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories
items.why: Apiiro's estimate comes via The Hacker News, which links it to North Korean actors; another source names no actor.
items.action: StepSecurity advises reviewing October workflow logs and pull-request timelines, requiring approval for workflows from external contributors, keeping VS Code in Restricted Mode for unfamiliar projects, and rotating GitHub, npm, SSH and cloud credentials from a clean machine if the loader ran.

items.title: Slovenian meat plant says hackers set a freezer to 100°C
items.why: Staff caught the change and no meat spoiled; the article names no culprit.
items.action: General advice: the article suggests inventorying OT assets, removing direct internet access to control equipment, and alerting on unexpected changes to target temperature settings.

items.title: SAP confirms suspicious activity; GitHub environment reportedly targeted
items.why: SAP says it found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data so far; Der Spiegel reports stolen employee tokens.
items.action: No action needed; for awareness. SAP says it has found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data so far.
